title: Price-concession triage and security-questionnaire integration for enterprise contract exceptions
creator: Priya Rao
description: Problem: Sales frequently submits MSA/DPA redlines that combine modest pricing concessions with small liability/indemnity tweaks and occasional security questionnaire (SSQ) exceptions. Manual legal review for each ticket increases cycle time and skews pricing experiments. Goal: Build an automated triage and soft-approval path that (1) quantifies concession budget impact on pricing experiments, (2) auto-approves low-risk concession requests within configurable thresholds, and (3) integrates SSQ answers to gate automated approvals. Scope: MVP covers MSA/DPA concessions related to liability caps, indemnity carve-outs, and data handling exceptions — and a mapping of 10 common SSQ questions to risk buckets. Success metrics: reduce legal review latency for eligible deals by 60%, decrease manual redline volume by 30% in Q2 trials, surface projected ARR impact per concession in the CRM UI.
acceptance_criteria: Concession scoring engine implemented that outputs: risk_score (0-100), estimated_unit_price_impact, recommended_approval_action (auto-approve / sales-escalate / legal-review)
SQ integration: top 10 SSQ question answers parsed and factored into risk_score; SSQ responses stored in contract ticket metadata
Auto-approval policy: configurable thresholds exist in console (by ARR, product tier, and concession dollar impact), and can be toggled per sales team
Telemetry: dashboard that shows percent auto-approved, avg legal time saved, and simulated revenue impact on current pricing experiments
Audit trail: every auto-approved concession produces a generated clause snippet and linked GitHub PR template or policy note for legal review later
Fallback: cases routed to legal queue include clear reason, priority flag, and suggested negotiation language
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with Legal (Anya Singh) and Sales Ops (Diego Morales). Agreed on 10 canonical SSQ questions and initial concession taxonomy.
2026-02-13: Data pull from CRM completed — sampled 180 recent redlines to derive distribution of concession sizes and typical liability language. Median concession impact = $18k ARR estimate.

2026-02-15: Prototype scoring model v0.1 implemented (features: concession_amount_pct_of_deal, requested_liability_cap_ratio, indemnity_scope_flag, SSQ_risk_count). Initial precision/recall on historical sample: 0.78 / 0.64 for low-risk auto-approvable cases.
2026-02-18: Design review with Console team. Added UI toggle for per-team policy and audit log link. Design feedback: show experiment-adjusted price delta rather than absolute $ in the first screen.
2026-02-20: Legal requested explicit handling for cross-border data transfer clauses; updated scope to include mapping of three DT clause variants. Marked security_review_required=true.
comments: Anya Singh (Legal): 'We can tolerate auto-approval for up to $50k one-off concessions when indemnity scope is narrow and SSQ answers show no critical findings.'
Diego Morales (Sales Ops): 'We need the estimated revenue impact in CRM so reps can see how a concession affects their quota attainment projections.'
Marcus Chen (Assignee): 'Will prototype a lightweight rule-engine + ML scorer. Plan: rules first (explicit deny/allow), then ML to rank uncertain cases.'
Priya Rao (Creator): 'Ensure experiments are gated so pricing analysis teams can run A/B on deals that used auto-approve vs. manual review.'
follow_up_tasks: Integrate scorer output into CRM deal workflow and add a 'simulate concession impact' button
Create legal review rotation for escalated cases and an SLA of 48 hours
Run pricing A/B experiment for 6 weeks comparing manual vs auto-approval outcomes
Expand SSQ mapping after 10-week pilot based on observed false positives
